newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Unwanted Swiss kiss goes French in Voltaire's town.
newsitem.headline: Unwanted Swiss kiss goes French in Voltaire's town.

text.p: The French town of Ferney-Voltaire has given artistic asylum to a Swiss sculpture of a naked couple kissing passionately, rejected by the authorities in Geneva.

The neighbouring town, where the great French thinker Voltaire spent 18 years of his life before his death in Paris in 1778, said it was giving asylum to the "kiss" with a "spirit of tolerance that was so dear to Voltaire and to Ferney."
The French literary icon Voltaire moved to Ferney-Voltaire in eastern France, bordering Geneva in French-speaking Switzerland, after he left the Calvinist city of Geneva in 1760.
Swiss artist Vincent Kesselring erected the seven-tonne marble "kiss" on an embankment on the shores of Lake Geneva in 1995.

But the Geneva authorities protested that he had not asked for permission to plant the "kiss", said they did not want the city to become a dumping ground for unauthorised works of art and ordered it removed last month.

Kesselring is now pressing for a popular vote in Geneva to support the return of his sculpture to the city. He has so far collected more than 6,000 signatures from the Swiss, who can have any issue put to the vote if they can assemble enough signatures.
